subject: Dedicated capacity: term length, proposed ramp schedule & discount scenarios
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Crane <tom.crane@averylabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: term length, proposed ramp schedule & discount scenarios

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together three pricing scenarios for Dedicated (reserved commit) that trade off term length, discount, and ramp speed. The attached pricing_scenarios.xlsx includes:

- Scenario A (12 months): smaller upfront commitment, 10% list discount, start-within-30-days, 2-week + 2-week staged ramp to full throughput; throughput guarantee: 95th percentile latency target and baseline token/sec per GPU.
- Scenario B (24 months): medium commit, 15% list discount, start-by-6-weeks, 4-week staged ramp; stronger throughput SLA and 1.5x burst capacity available.
- Scenario C (36 months): largest commit, 22% list discount, 8-week ramp, reserved GPU pool sizing recommendations (8 x A100-class GPUs or equivalent); includes extended billing credits for SLA misses.

Questions we need answered to firm a proposal:
- Preferred term (12/24/36)?
- Target production start date (earliest date you can commit to for network provisioning / security review)?
- Throughput target in tokens/sec or expected peak RPS so we can size GPU pool (I put a few example workload profiles in the sheet).
- Anything in procurement template that will change invoice/payment terms (Net30 vs Net45) or require additional PO fields?

If it helps, our recommended baseline for a predictable 99ms median generation on your LLM family is an 8-GPU pool with autoscaling headroom for spikes — we called that out in the 36-month scenario.

I've CC'd Ben (finance) and Marissa (legal) to raise any constraints on discount floors and redlines. Look forward to your feedback — happy to walk the scenarios on a quick follow-up.

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: pricing_scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet with cost/throughput/ramp comparisons)

From: Tom Crane <tom.crane@averylabs.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@averylabs.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: term length, proposed ramp schedule & discount scenarios

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. We've reviewed Scenario A/B/C internally. A few initial items:

1) Term: Preference toward 24 months (Scenario B) because it balances commitment and flexibility for our product roadmap.
2) Start date: we'd like a firm production start by May 15, 2026 if possible — will that work with your provisioning and security checks?
3) Throughput: current steady-state is ~45 requests/min with average 220 tokens per request; peak tested at 3x. We want headroom for 3x peaks. Please translate into GPU sizing — the spreadsheet is helpful but can you confirm exact GPU counts?
4) Invoice / Payment: Avery prefers Net30 and we need standard PO fields. Also procurement will ask for SLA credit language: if you miss throughput or availability SLAs we expect a credit equal to the proportionate monthly fee up to a cap. Please indicate your position.

I attached our standard procurement_template.pdf for reference — it has our vendor onboarding checklist and PO instructions. Once we align on term and SLA we can move to legal redlines.

Tom Crane
Head of Platform Ops, Avery Labs
tom.crane@averylabs.com

Attachments: procurement_template.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: term length, proposed ramp schedule & discount scenarios

Ben / Marissa —

FYI: Tom at Avery prefers 24 months and a May 15 production start. They want Net30 and an SLA credit construct (cap to be negotiated). Please see Tom's notes and the procurement template attached to his reply. Key asks for ops/finance/legal:

- Ben: is 15% discount (Scenario B) the floor we can offer for a 24-month commit? Any requirement for upfront deposit or monthly billing? They want a clear cap on SLA credits (we normally cap at one month's committed spend, but curious if finance will push).
- Marissa: procurement_template has standard confidentiality and indemnity asks; also they will push for firm throughput/availability language. Can you propose redlines (I suggested a targeted SLA credit of up to 30% of a missed-month fee in our internal model, with 48h notice requirement before credits apply).

I attached the pricing_scenarios.xlsx they were sent and their procurement PDF.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if helpful.

—Naomi

Attachments forwarded: pricing_scenarios.xlsx, procurement_template.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: term length, proposed ramp schedule & discount scenarios

Naomi —

Looks reasonable. For finance: 24-month with a 15% list discount is acceptable if we get either (a) a 3-month minimum billing guarantee up front or (b) a modest upfront deposit equal to one month of committed spend. Net30 is fine.

SLA credits: Finance is comfortable with a capped credit up to one monthly committed fee for availability/throughput misses — less than our Scenario C language but standard for us. If marketing/legal want to make the credit more nuanced (sliding scale by severity), we can accept that but prefer the cap.

Ramp: Recommend a 6-week ramp (2-week staging + 4-week throughput increase) before we declare full production SLA to give time for KV caching and tokenization tuning. I've attached a quick capacity_plan.xlsx showing how 8 GPUs map to their workload with 3x headroom.

Ben
VP, Finance Operations
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: capacity_plan.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: term length, proposed ramp schedule & discount scenarios

Team —

Reviewed procurement_template.pdf. A few legal redlines I'll want to make before we send a revised commercial term sheet to Avery:

1) SLA language: define measurable KPIs (p95 latency, error-rate, successful token generation rate) and explicitly exclude outages caused by customer-side misconfiguration or third-party network events.
2) SLA credits: accept a capped credit up to one monthly committed fee (aligns with Ben), but add a 30-day remediation clause and a maximum of two consecutive creditable events.
3) Security & Data: we need to preserve our standard customer data processing addendum; for Dedicated deployments, confirm whether they need on-prem keys or a customer-managed KMS.

I'll draft commit_term_redlines.pdf with specific clause language. Once Naomi confirms the start date and Ben confirms the deposit approach, I can finalize redlines for their review.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: commit_term_redlines.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Crane <tom.crane@averylabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: term length, proposed ramp schedule & discount scenarios

Tom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. To summarize and propose a next step:

- Term: we can proceed on a 24-month reserved commit with a 15% list discount (Scenario B).
- Billing: Net30 accepted. We typically ask for either a one-month upfront deposit or a 3-month minimum billing guarantee; please let us know which you prefer.
- Start date & ramp: We can target a May 15, 2026 production start, with a 6-week ramp (2-week staging + 4-week scale to full throughput). Ben's capacity plan maps your stated request (45 req/min, 220 tokens/req, 3x peaks) to an 8-GPU pool with autoscaling headroom.
- SLA & credits: Legal is proposing redlines that define KPIs and a credit cap equal to one monthly committed fee; they'll add remediation windows and exclusions. Marissa will send a redline PDF for your review.

I've attached a revised pricing workbook (20260301-pricing_revision.xlsx) that reflects the 24-month/15% pricing and the 6-week ramp milestone dates. Next steps if that aligns with you:
1) Confirm preferred billing guarantee (upfront deposit vs 3-month minimum).
2) Confirm DocuSign path for our SOW + commitment schedule.
3) We'll schedule a technical kickoff for week of Apr 20 to run security onboarding and capacity validation.

If you confirm the above, Ben and Marissa will prepare the commercial and legal package and we'll circulate for signature. Happy to jump on a 20-min call to finalize.

Best,
Naomi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Attachments: 20260301-pricing_revision.xlsx
